about.title: Santa Monica Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can fail almost anywhere in Santa Monica: a space heater in an apartment off Lincoln Boulevard, an e-bike battery near the beach path, a brake or airbag component on Pacific Coast Highway or the I-10. What matters under California law is simpler than most people expect. Product cases usually rest on strict liability, which means you generally do not have to prove the company was careless. You show the product had a defect in how it was designed, how it was built, or how it was labeled, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach past the manufacturer to the distributor and the retailer. Santa Monica sits in Los Angeles County, and claims from the city move through that county's court system. LawProactive is not a law firm and does not handle your claim. We are a free service that matches you with an independent attorney who takes product cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless something is recovered. Hold on to the product, its packaging, and your receipts.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Monica Residents Use LawProactive for Product Cases

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In most California product cases you do not need to prove the maker was negligent, only that the product was defective and the defect injured you. The attorneys we connect you with build claims around that standard.

items.title: Three kinds of defect, one claim
items.desc: Design flaws, manufacturing errors, and missing or inadequate warnings are each a valid basis for liability in California. An attorney can sort out which applies to what happened to you.

items.title: Every link in the chain can answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer who sold the item may all share liability under California law. Your attorney can identify each of them, and there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My crash on Pacific Coast Highway involved an airbag that never deployed. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Santa Monica recorded 445 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve a vehicle component that failed rather than, or in addition to, a driver's mistake. A product liability claim against the manufacturer can run alongside a claim against another driver. Do not let the car be scrapped or repaired until an attorney has had a chance to preserve the evidence.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Usually not. California applies strict liability to most product defect claims, so the focus is on whether the product was defective and whether that defect caused your injury. Whether the company acted carelessly is generally not something you have to establish.

items.question: I threw away the broken product. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, but the product itself is often the strongest evidence, so its absence makes the case harder. Photos, the packaging, receipts, purchase records, and medical documentation can still help. Talk with an attorney before assuming the claim is gone.
